Wadi Ghadir · Eastern Desert, Egypt · SimPEG 0.25

Wadi Ghadir SimPEG Inversions

Three Jupyter notebooks invert the Wadi Ghadir survey in 3-D on one common mesh below the Copernicus topography: the complete Bouguer anomaly for density, the total-field magnetic anomaly for susceptibility, and both together, coupled by a cross-gradient term so that the two models share their structure. All models are compact: sparse norms (p = 0 on the values, 1 on the gradients) solved by iteratively re-weighted least squares, with the smooth L2 models kept for comparison.

Written by Mohamed Sobh, LIAG · Leibniz Institute for Applied Geophysics, Hannover

Density from gravity

The compact model concentrates the anomalous mass in a few bodies with sharp edges: dense bodies (red) through the centre and north of the survey, light bodies (blue) along its western and eastern margins. They reach the bounds of ±0.3 g/cm³ relative to 2.67 g/cm³, where the smooth model spreads ±0.1 g/cm³ over large volumes.

Susceptibility from magnetics

The compact susceptibility model reduces the magnetic sources to a few small bodies that reach the bound of 0.3 SI: below the strongest anomaly in the south-west (down to about 1 km depth), shallow ones in the east and north-west, and deeper ones in the centre (about 691 km E, 2742 km N). Where an induced body sits below the ground, the reduced-to-pole map of the magnetic chain shows its high.

Joint inversion

The compact joint inversion uses one trade-off parameter β for both data sets and stops when their total misfit reaches the number of data: gravity ends a little below its target (χ² 0.56) and magnetics a little above (χ² 1.26). The boundaries of the two models now coincide: the gradient-weighted structural dissimilarity falls from 0.26 to 0.073 (72 % lower). Values are not tied together: a dense body may be magnetic or not.

Choosing the coupling weight λ

Test runs of the smooth joint inversion (25 iterations each). λ = 10⁹ is the strongest coupling that still fits both data sets; the compact joint inversion uses the same value.

Reading the models

Potential-field data do not determine a unique model. The compact inversions return the model with the fewest anomalous cells and sharp edges that fits the data; the smooth inversions the smallest and smoothest. Both fit equally well, so shapes and depths depend on this choice: compare them before interpreting a body.

The magnetic models assume induced magnetisation along today's field (IGRF-14, survey date assumed 20 January 2026); remanence would move or reshape the bodies. Cells far from the data are unconstrained and are blanked in the slices.

Mesh: 400 m × 400 m × 100 m core cells, 81 × 57 × 28 cells, 105,895 below the Copernicus GLO-30 topography. Models are exported as NumPy and UBC-GIF files in outputs/inversion/; shared code in wghadir/inversion.py.
